what: The heuristic precomputes the CVRP structure once in new(): it identifies the depot and customers from loc/visited fact names, extracts grounded operator costs to build a directed shortest-path distance matrix, and looks up load(), vehicles(), capacity(), max_vehicles(), and demand(c) exactly by name with permissive defaults if missing. For each state it reads the current location, load, vehicles-used, and unvisited customers; if all customers are visited it returns the remaining return-to-depot cost. Otherwise it computes two constructive CVRP upper bounds: (1) a capacity- and vehicle-limited nearest-neighbor completion from the current route, and (2) a Clarke-Wright savings solution from the depot after optionally closing the current route immediately. It returns the minimum of these two feasible completion costs.
why: CVRP remaining cost is dominated by routing decisions constrained by capacity and the number of vehicles. Grounded operator costs provide exact route costs without fragile parsing of derived travel-cost variables. The nearest-neighbor estimate uses the current load and current customer location, while Clarke-Wright savings captures good merging decisions for the remaining customers. Taking the minimum of two feasible constructive estimates tightens the heuristic without sacrificing feasibility, and all expensive distance/operator processing is done once in new(), so per-state evaluation is O(n^2) and fast enough for search.
